newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France to sell 20 pct of France Telecom in April.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France to sell 20 pct of France Telecom in April.

text.p: Telecoms minister Francois Fillon said in an interview published on Tuesday France will sell 20 percent of state-owned France Telecom next April in what analysts say will be the country's biggest ever stock market operation.
The first tranche of 20 percent tranche, mainly aimed at private individuals, will be sold in the first half of April 1997, he said in the interview with the newspaper La Tribune.

He also said wanted to see a third competitor in the French telecoms sector, alongside France Telecom and the recently formed grouping of Generale des Eaux, British Telecom Plc, SBC Communications Corp and Mannesmann AG.
The minister's remarks on the partial sale of France Telecom, confirm recent suggestions from Chairman Michel Bon who said he expected a first tranche to be sold in April.

A spokeswoman at Fillon's ministry was not immediately available to comment on the timing of the second tranche, which analysts said was now unlikely to take place before the full liberalisation of the European telecommunications sector in 1998.
The French government has said it will sell a total of 49 percent of France Telecom, with 10 percent earmarked for France Telecom staff.
"The first tranche due in the second half of April (1997), should cover about 20 percent of the capital," Fillon said in the interview.
"The general idea is to carry out the largest public offering ever in France. France Telecom has 32 million customers, that's a fantastic starting point."
"Our target is to be at least as ambitious as Deutsche Telekom, which is aiming for two million individual shareholders," Fillon said.
He said 20 percent of France Telecom's capital was a big amount to reserve for a cross-shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, but added that it was too soon to tell what the right amount should be.

"Before deciding on the cross-shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, we must know the value of the German and French operators. Taking into account the foreseeable value of the companies, 20 percent seems to me financially high," he said.
Fillon said he was pleased at General des Eaux's creation of the Cegetel telecoms grouping but said a third big company was desirable to ensure competition played its part in the market.

"We had the example of mobile telephones, a sector where it took a third competitor for competition to play its full role and for the market to develop," he said. "I would like therefore to see a third operator created."
